provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Clean family batch, book archetype. Mid-size residential tickets with seasonal spikes and repeat cleans, so products lean on reminders, photo quotes and rug intake. No equipment or solution brands. Fresh Fern fails CTA contrast. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How urine spots are found, when the pad or subfloor needs treating, what an odour treatment can and can't promise, and pricing per spot or per room
pageStructurePlus.why: Pet owners search for the problem, not for carpet cleaning. An honest page about urine and odour is the one they book from.

pageStructurePlus.section: Area rug pickup and in-plant washing
pageStructurePlus.contains: Which rugs get washed in the plant versus cleaned on site, wool, silk and synthetic, fringe work, how to measure a rug, and the pickup and return window
pageStructurePlus.why: Rug owners are careful and want the process in writing before a stranger rolls up a rug they love.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What the cleaning code on a sofa tag means, which fabrics get wet or dry cleaning, microfiber, leather and mattresses, and when a test spot comes first
pageStructurePlus.why: People worry a cleaner will ruin a sofa. Explaining fabric codes shows the upholstery is in careful hands.

pageStructurePlus.section: Drying time and the day of the clean
pageStructurePlus.contains: Typical drying hours, walking on damp carpet, which furniture gets moved and blocked, driveway and hose access for the truck, and fans on request
pageStructurePlus.why: The questions that stall a carpet cleaning booking are practical: can the kids walk on it tonight, and where does the truck park.

pageStructurePlus.section: Tile and grout cleaning and sealing
pageStructurePlus.contains: Kitchen and bathroom tile, grout colour sealing, shower walls, natural stone limits, and before-and-after shots by room
pageStructurePlus.why: Tile and grout is a separate search with a separate buyer. A page of its own catches the kitchen job carpet pages never mention.

designDirections.name: Per-Room Price

designDirections.headlineSample: Carpet cleaning in {City}, priced per room
designDirections.whyItFits: Citrus Morning's warm orange button and geometric headings feel energetic and clean, and make a per-room price impossible to miss.

designDirections.name: Before and After, Then Book
designDirections.bestFor: Carpet and upholstery companies with a steady before-and-after habit and a calendar to fill

designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Fresh Fern, fails CTA contrast. Teal & Tangerine keeps the fresh feel with a teal button that passes, and its humanist type stays friendly.

designDirections.name: The Rug Room
designDirections.bestFor: Established firms with an in-plant rug wash and fine upholstery work for designers and careful owners
designDirections.headlineSample: Fine rug and upholstery cleaning for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: Cacao's deep brown and bookish serif feel like a rug workshop, which suits owners handing over wool, silk and heirloom pieces.

openers.line: Your listing has strong carpet cleaning reviews but no Website button, so someone staring at a red wine spill at 9pm has nowhere to see what a room costs.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Where that carpet spill search could land: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens Facebook, where the per-room carpet cleaning special is buried under a dozen other posts. A new customer has to scroll to find a price.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link. Note where it lands and how far down the newest price post sits.
openers.linkLine: Your carpet cleaning prices on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing still shows a carpet cleaning coupon that ran out, and the booking form doesn't send. That visitor called the next cleaner instead.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale thing: an expired coupon, a dead form, an old number. Write it down.
openers.linkLine: The same carpet cleaner, with a booking form that works: {demo-link}

openers.line: On my phone your carpet cleaning page loads sideways and the Book button hides under a banner. People book this from the room with the stain, phone in hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Carpet cleaning, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing online says what a room of carpet or a three-seat sofa costs, so the shopper who just wanted a number books whichever upholstery cleaner posts one.
openers.hook: Check the listing, posts and any site for a per-room or per-piece price. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A price per room and per sofa, bookable: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your videos of the dirty extraction water are the most convincing carpet cleaning proof there is, and they drop off the feed in a few days.
openers.hook: Find one dirty-water or split-carpet post and note the room. Mention it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: A before-and-after carpet gallery that stays put: {demo-link}

openers.line: Several of your reviews thank you for getting dog accidents out of the carpet. Pet owners searching for that exact problem should land on a page built around it.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and find one about pets, urine or odour. Quote the phrase back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: A pet odour page built on your carpet reviews: {demo-link}

openers.line: Carpet and upholstery bookings bunch up before Thanksgiving, and the cleaner whose open days are visible fills the calendar first.
openers.hook: Use from mid-October to late November. Check for a post about holiday openings or being booked out.
openers.linkLine: Pre-holiday carpet cleaning with open days showing: {demo-link}

openers.line: You mention washing area rugs, but there's no way to book a rug pickup or see what a wool rug costs. Rug owners want that in writing before they hand one over.
openers.hook: Look for 'rug' in their services, posts or reviews. Only use this if rug cleaning shows up.
openers.linkLine: Rug pickup and washing, booked online: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a carpet cleaning technician. Good applicants look at the company and the truck online before they call about the job.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign on the truck. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A carpet cleaning page with a technician hiring section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews come from {Neighborhood} and a few towns over, but nothing online says how far the carpet cleaning truck goes, so people at the edge never ask.
openers.hook: Find the furthest town mentioned in their reviews or posts and use it.
openers.linkLine: A coverage page for the carpet cleaning truck: {demo-link}

openers.line: Tenants moving out search for carpet cleaning with a receipt for the landlord. A move-out page with a fixed price per room and an emailed receipt catches them.
openers.hook: Use from May to August, or if they mention apartments or rentals in posts.
openers.linkLine: Move-out carpet cleaning with a receipt for the landlord: {demo-link}

openers.line: Moving someone's sofa and running hoses through their front door is a trust decision. If you're insured, say it on the page beside the carpet cleaning price.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured' on their listing, truck or posts. Never claim what you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and care promises on one carpet page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your carpet cleaning runs on repeat customers and word of mouth. That holds until a regular moves away and the new owner searches instead.
openers.hook: Look for reviews that say 'every year' or 'second time'. Quote one.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred carpet customer should land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted shows what a proper carpet extraction does. It belongs on a page the next person can book from.
openers.hook: Pick their newest carpet, rug or upholstery post and name it: the room, the stain, the piece.
openers.linkLine: That carpet job on a page that books: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is a great carpet result.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the Facebook page, but nowhere to see a price per room or book a cleaning. I put together a sample site with room and sofa prices, a pet odour page and a booking calendar, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample carpet and upholstery cleaning site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has a price per room and per sofa, a pet odour page, rug pickup booking and drying-time answers. If it's not useful, tell me and I'll leave you alone.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for carpet cleaning companies here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss from the truck. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with a price per room, a pet odour page and online booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a carpet cleaner your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}, a few whole-house jobs."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, maybe between jobs?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: Most of my work is repeat customers.
objections.handler: "Good, that means the carpet cleaning is right. The site sends them a reminder when it's been a year and lets their neighbour book without calling you."

objections.objection: I can't price online, every carpet is different.
objections.handler: "Show a per-room starting price and say heavy soil or pet treatment is extra after you look. The shoppers who only want a number stop calling, and the real jobs still come in."
"That's why now. The site goes live before the pre-holiday rush, and the slow weeks are when the rug and tile pages have time to start showing up."

objections.objection: I'm already paying for leads from an app.
objections.handler: "App leads go to several carpet cleaners at once and you pay either way. Someone who finds your own site only gets you."
"Keep him on it if he likes it. What's missing is a room price, pet odour answers and a booking calendar. I can add those or build alongside him."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's the price list, booking, the pet odour page and rug pickup. That's a few whole-house carpet jobs."

email.subject: Carpet cleaning site for {Business Name}

{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} carpet cleaning demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — the pre-holiday carpet rush in {City} is close, and people book whoever shows open days first. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a few whole-house carpet jobs, not to a single room special.
The per-room and per-piece price list is the core. Price rug, tile and pet pages as additions.
Price the rug page higher when it includes pickup scheduling and an intake form; that's real workflow.
Charge per page for tile and grout, commercial carpet and move-out; each one brings its own buyer.
Keep monthly items under the price of one room, so they never feel like a lost job.
A before-and-after gallery is worth more when it is sorted by problem: pets, traffic lanes, wine, rugs.

lineItems.description: Max with room, stair, hallway, sofa, chair and mattress prices, pet treatment add-ons and a minimum charge shown clearly.

lineItems.item: Rug pickup booking and intake form
lineItems.description: Max with rug size and fibre questions, condition notes, a pickup window picker and a texted pickup receipt.
Max with a short odour question set, per-spot pricing and honest notes on when the pad or subfloor is involved.
Max with grout sealing options, shower and kitchen pricing and a room-sorted before-and-after set.
Max with a quarterly schedule request form, after-hours options and an office-sized price guide.
Max with filters for pets, traffic lanes, spills, rugs and upholstery, and short captions per job.

lineItems.item: Town pages for the truck's range (each)
lineItems.description: Max when each page names the neighbourhoods covered, any trip charge and reviews from that town.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep with carpet before-and-afters
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A real split-carpet before-and-after on your Google profile every week, so the listing shows the work instead of just the phone number."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests that ask about the stain
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day after each carpet job, a short note asks the customer to mention what you got out. Those words are what the next pet owner searches."

whatElseYouSell.name: Pre-holiday and spring carpet campaigns
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Two campaigns a year to past carpet customers and their neighbours: before the holidays and after the muddy season."

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck wrap and door hanger artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The truck parks in a driveway for two hours on every carpet job. Artwork with the booking address on it turns that into a sign the street reads."
whatElseYouSell.when: Right after launch, coordinated with their wrap shop.

whatElseYouSell.name: Rug wash photo and video day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Half a day filming a rug going through the wash and dust removal gives the rug page something no other carpet cleaner in town has."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, if they wash rugs in a plant or a shop.

whatElseYouSell.name: Landlord and leasing office move-out flyer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A move-out carpet cleaning sheet for leasing offices, with the per-room price and the receipt promise, so tenants call you first."

whatElseYouSell.name: Annual re-clean postcard
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A postcard eleven months after each carpet clean, with the same technician's name and a booking address, for customers who ignore texts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once there's a year of past jobs to mail.

withoutAI.route: House cleaners who refer carpet work
withoutAI.whoPays: The house cleaning company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Which house cleaners send you carpet jobs? They need a booking site too, and your word gets me in."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Cleaners and carpet companies trade customers constantly and trust each other's recommendations.

withoutAI.route: Flooring stores that sell the carpet
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The flooring store that recommends you for carpet care has a catalog nobody can browse on a phone. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Flooring stores have bigger budgets and already send buyers to the carpet cleaner after install.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The restoration company you help on flooded carpet jobs needs an emergency page that works at 2am. I can build it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Restoration firms have insurance-funded work and value the carpet cleaners who show up for them.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your apartment manager's leasing site can't show a vacant unit with clean carpet photos or take a tour request. That's my next build."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers trust the vendor who turns units around, and that trust gets a meeting.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The upholstery shop you send torn sofas to, and that sends you dirty ones, shows its work on Facebook only. Same fix."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Upholsterers and cleaners share customers and refer each other both ways.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The designer who sends you wool rugs before a photo shoot needs a portfolio that isn't a feed. Your rug work proves I get detail."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Designers pay for portfolios and trust the rug cleaner who handles their clients' pieces.

withAI.route: Care guide assistant for the flooring store
withAI.pitchLine: "New carpet buyers ask how to treat a spill or when to deep clean, and the assistant answers from the store's care sheets and books the carpet cleaner."
withAI.whyItWorks: Stores want fewer callbacks after install, and the cleaner gets the bookings.

withAI.route: Flood claim photo log for the restoration company
withAI.pitchLine: "Technicians photograph wet carpet and pad room by room, and the log writes the notes the adjuster asks for."
withAI.whyItWorks: Restoration firms live and die on documentation, and the carpet client's introduction opens the door.

withAI.pitchLine: "Tenants ask what the carpet needs before move-out, and the assistant answers from the lease checklist and offers a cleaning slot."
withAI.whyItWorks: Landlords repeat the same deposit answers every month and pay to stop.

withAI.route: Fabric-care answers for the furniture shop
withAI.pitchLine: "Sofa buyers ask what the cleaning code on the tag means, and the assistant answers from the shop's fabric sheets and books the upholstery cleaner."
withAI.whyItWorks: Shops field fabric questions daily, and the cleaner earns the follow-on work.

withAI.route: Photo quote helper for house cleaners
withAI.pitchLine: "House cleaning clients send a picture of the kitchen, and the cleaner gets a draft deep clean price, same tool I built for carpet quotes."
withAI.whyItWorks: It already runs for a carpet business the house cleaner trusts.

withAI.route: Rug sourcing notes for interior designers
withAI.pitchLine: "Designers keep each client's rugs, fibres, sizes and last cleaning date in one place, and get a nudge when a rug is due a wash."
withAI.whyItWorks: Designers track pieces across many homes, and the rug cleaner benefits from every reminder.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back with room prices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The wand is running and the phone rings. The caller gets a text with your per-room carpet prices and a booking link before you shut the machine off."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Twelve-month carpet re-clean reminder
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A year after each carpet clean, the customer gets a text with last year's rooms already filled in and the same technician's next open day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a list of past jobs with dates and rooms.

softwareAI.name: Drying and aftercare text
softwareAI.pitchLine: "As the truck pulls away, the customer gets drying times, when to put furniture back and what to do if a spot wicks back up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the owner's aftercare instructions per service.

softwareAI.name: Photo quote for stains, rooms and sofas
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Customers send a few pictures of the stained carpet or the sofa, and you get a draft upholstery or carpet quote from your own prices to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the price list and a set of past jobs with photos and final prices. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Rug intake tracker with tags and condition notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every rug picked up gets a tag, size, fibre, condition notes and pictures, so you always know which rug is in the wash and when it goes home."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their rug intake routine and a phone for the pickup driver.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for carpet jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every carpet cleaning review gets a reply in your voice that names the room or the stain, ready for you to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job ticket with pre-existing damage sign-off
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before the wand touches the carpet, the technician notes worn spots, loose seams and fabric codes, and the customer signs on the phone."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their walk-through checklist and the wording they use today.

softwareAI.name: Booking chat for carpet and upholstery questions
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'can you do a microfiber sectional' and 'how long until we can walk on it' from your answers, then books the carpet cleaning slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs services, prices, drying answers and the calendar. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Truck route planner by town
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Carpet jobs grouped by town and day, so the truck isn't crossing the county between a two-room job and a sofa."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs job addresses, job lengths and the trucks they run.

softwareAI.name: After-hours receptionist for spill and pet calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone calls at night about a dog accident on new carpet, gets calm first-aid steps you approved, and books the first morning slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the calendar, prices and the owner's approved spill advice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Commercial carpet schedule for offices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each office's carpet cleaning dates, traffic lanes and after-hours access in one schedule, with the manager reminded the week before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, once they have a few commercial accounts. Needs the account list and frequencies.

softwareAI.name: Technician applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "People applying for carpet cleaning technician jobs answer your questions about licences, lifting and early starts, and you only call the good fits."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any month they're hiring. Needs must-haves, pay and schedule. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Pet treatment record per home
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Which rooms had urine treatment, which spots came back and what was used, so the next carpet visit starts where the last one stopped."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the job ticket and their treatment notes.

softwareAI.name: Rug condition notes from pickup pictures
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The driver photographs a rug at pickup and gets draft condition notes, fringe wear, moth damage, colour run, to check and send the owner."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the rug intake tracker. Needs past intake notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per truck day
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which carpet jobs pay once drive time, solution and labour are counted, so the minimum charge is set from your numbers."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a few months of job times and supply costs.

softwareAI.name: Customer message sorter for carpet jobs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Reschedules, 'the spot came back' messages and rug pickup questions get sorted and drafted, so the owner clears the inbox from the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the business text line or inbox. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Cleaning solution and supply log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Which pre-sprays and rinses each truck carries, when they run low and the safety sheets, ready when a carpet customer asks what you used."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their product list per truck.

softwareAI.name: Office carpet bid writer
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through an office walk-through and get a draft commercial carpet cleaning bid with frequency and price to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs past office bids and their rates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Rug pickup and return texts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Rug owners get a text when the rug is picked up, when it's washed and drying, and the morning it comes home, so nobody calls asking where their rug is."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the rug intake tracker. Needs the tracker's status steps and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Win-back for carpet customers past two years
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A list of carpet customers who haven't booked in two years, sorted by neighbourhood, with a ready offer to send when the calendar has gaps."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their customer history export.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the rug intake tracker for rug cleaners
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Rug and carpet cleaning companies, monthly per account
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a rug intake and tracking tool for one carpet cleaner. Every shop that washes rugs loses track of whose rug is where."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the workflow, and every rug-washing shop has the same tag-and-return problem.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: License the room price list to a cleaning solution distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every carpet cleaner who buys pre-spray from you a booking site with room pricing, and they reorder from you without thinking."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want owner-operators loyal, and a daily tool beats a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member carpet cleaner a booking template with a pet odour page and drying answers as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and one agreement reaches many owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each of your carpet cleaning territories needs room prices, town pages and a booking calendar that routes to the right truck."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract, many territories, one template built on a real owner-operator's site.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The training school, per class or flat fee
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every new carpet cleaner leaving your class needs a site with room prices on day one. Bundle my template with the course."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Schools sell to new owners who all need the same site, and the school brings the buyers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label carpet cleaning template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency keeps building carpet cleaning sites from scratch. License my template with room pricing and the pet odour page done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies sell the client; you sell them the part you've already perfected.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Carpet care referral page for flooring retail chains
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every carpet you sell needs cleaning eventually. One care page per store with vetted local carpet cleaners and a booking button."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chains want buyers happy after install, and the referral page is a service they can name at the register.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Turnover carpet program for apartment operators
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every vacant unit gets its carpet cleaning booked from one board, with receipts filed for the deposit dispute."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Operators turn units every month and pay to stop chasing vendors by phone.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Subcontractor network page for restoration firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your flood jobs need carpet cleaners on call. One page where vetted carpet subs sign up and get dispatched."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Restoration firms need reliable subs in a hurry, and the carpet client is the first one on the list.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same carpet cleaning stack in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New carpet cleaning clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one carpet cleaner per area, and {City} has one. Your county is still open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the room price list, the pet page and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rug dealers' care and cleaning program
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every rug you sell gets a care card that books its first wash with a trusted rug cleaner a year later."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Dealers want a reason for buyers to come back, and the cleaner earns the wash.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Rescue unfinished carpet cleaning booking builds
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started your carpet booking or rug tracking tool and disappeared. I've shipped that flow for another cleaner."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded owners already decided to buy; they want someone who has finished one.

upsellLadder.offer: Carpet cleaning booking site plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The carpet site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new room price or a holiday special is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Review requests that ask about the stain
upsellLadder.trigger: A month live, and a customer has thanked them for a stain or pet result.
upsellLadder.line: "That customer who couldn't believe the stain came out should say it where the next carpet shopper reads it."

upsellLadder.trigger: They share a past job list, or mention customers who come back every year.
upsellLadder.line: "Your yearly carpet customers shouldn't have to remember you. The reminder remembers for them."

upsellLadder.offer: Photo quote for stains, rooms and sofas
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of booking messages show people sending pictures and asking for a price.
upsellLadder.line: "People are already sending pictures of the sofa. Let the photo quote draft the upholstery price before you call back."

upsellLadder.offer: Rug intake tracker with tags and condition notes
upsellLadder.trigger: Rug pickups come through the site, or they mention a rug that went missing in the shop.
upsellLadder.line: "Once rugs start coming in from the site, every rug needs a tag and a status. Let's track them."

upsellLadder.trigger: Six weeks before the pre-holiday rush or the spring thaw.
upsellLadder.line: "The carpet rush is coming. Let's send past customers the open days before they call someone else."

upsellLadder.trigger: They land a second office or a property manager asks for a quarterly carpet schedule.
upsellLadder.line: "Two offices on a quarterly carpet schedule is a calendar problem already. Put them in one place."
